results.summary_before: This design compares the behavior of OR versus XOR gates and AND versus NAND gates. Inputs 0 and 1 are fed to OR and XOR gates, while inputs 2 and 3 are fed to AND and NAND gates. The outputs can be observed with a seven-segment display or other indicators. The project is educational, highlighting the similarities and differences between these gate types.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design implements an 8-bit priority encoder that converts the highest-priority set bit into a decimal digit displayed on a 7-segment display. If no bits are set, a decimal point is shown instead of a digit. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware beyond the 7-segment display and input switches. It is a simple educational project for demonstrating priority encoding and 7-segment decoding.

results.summary_before: The project implements a monophonic keyboard synthesizer with one octave of notes, generating sine waves using an efficient delta-step method. The 8-bit output is provided directly and also via a PWM generator for audio output, intended for use with Mike Bell's audio PMOD. Testing involves attaching the input PMOD to a row of buttons for playing notes. No silicon test results are mentioned.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design is a streaming multiply-accumulate unit supporting the OCP MXFP8 microscaling formats, including E4M3 and E5M2, with hardware-accelerated shared scaling for AI inference. It receives two 8-bit data streams on the input and bidirectional pins and produces an 8-bit output stream. A Tiny Tapeout DevKit with a provided MicroPython driver can be used for quick prototyping, while a Sipeed Tang Nano 4K with an FPGA bitstream and Cortex-M3 testbench is available for high-speed testing. The design is notable for implementing a compact floating-point MAC core for sub-8-bit AI workloads.

results.summary_before: Tiny Shader is a programmable shader unit that executes a 10-instruction shader per pixel to generate images and animations, output via VGA at 640x480 with an internal resolution of 64x48. It includes an SPI interface for loading new shaders and setting a user register. Testing requires a Tiny VGA Pmod and optionally an SPI controller. Silicon testing confirmed all features work, including custom shader upload and animation.

results.summary_before: This project implements a generic synchronous FIFO buffer with a single clock domain. It buffers data from an 8-bit input to an 8-bit output, with write and read enable signals and full/empty flags. The design is intended as an experimental microtile container. Testing involves writing data until full and reading until empty.
